label: Prove FTC Part 2 using a partition, the Mean Value Theorem, and a telescoping sum
steps: Take a regular partition P={x_i} of [a,b].
Apply the Mean Value Theorem on each subinterval [x_{i-1},x_i] to find c_i with F(x_i)−F(x_{i-1})=f(c_i)Δx.
Sum over i to get a telescoping sum equal to F(b)−F(a).
Take the limit as n→∞; the sum tends to the definite integral of f over [a,b].
success_criteria: Derivation establishes the evaluation theorem for continuous f and any antiderivative F.

scope.text: Calculus; f continuous on [a,b]; F an antiderivative of f

notes: Reusable proof method. The specific derivation/walkthrough is recorded separately as Study (study:proof:ftc-part2).
